records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.java:124 leaves previous local recovery codes intact after successfully storing replacements externally, allowing old codes to remain valid through local-provider fallback. Remove the previous local credential when external replacement succeeds.
records.rationale: The finding describes a real issue in the new createRecoveryCodesCredential method (lines 112-129). When userStorageCreated is true (external storage succeeds), the method returns without removing any existing local credentials. The else branch only creates a new local credential when external storage fails. records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 validates recovery codes without persisting consumption, allowing indefinite replay and incorrectly reporting all codes as remaining. Persist consumption and test replay rejection.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() at line 283-305 validates recovery codes by checking if the input matches any code in the stored list (line 305: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`), but does NOT remove or mark the used code as consumed. This means the same code can be validated multiple times. However, this is a TEST provider (in testsuite-providers), not production code. records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:getCredentials returns a legacy OTP model with unset credentialData and secretData, causing OTP deserialization to fail during account credential listing. Convert it to a modern OTP credential model before returning it.
